title: How the Copilot Creators Collective is shaping the future of creativity and AI literacy
summary: Discover how Microsoft's Copilot Creators Collective is helping Filipino creators advance AI literacy, responsible AI use, and creative innovation.
body_markdown:
A year ago, Microsoft brought together a group of Filipino creators around a shared question: what becomes possible when creativity, community, and AI come together?


That question became the starting point for the Copilot Creators Collective, a community built around a clear mission: to help more Filipinos understand, explore, and use AI responsibly through the voices of creators they trust.


One year later, that mission has been brought to life by CCC members who are not only experimenting with Microsoft Copilot in their own work, but also translating AI into stories, conversations, and learning moments that feel practical, familiar, and human.


At the heart of the Collective is Microsoft’s vision of empowering every person and organization on the planet to achieve more. For the CCC, that vision extends from creators to the communities they reach. Through campaigns, learning sessions, and creator-led storytelling, members have helped broaden AI literacy and advocate for responsible AI use by showing how Copilot can support real moments in work, life, education, creativity, and learning.


“Over the past year, the Copilot Creators Collective has shown us what happens when Filipino creators are given the space, tools, and community to explore AI with purpose,” said Josh Aquino, Head of Communication of Microsoft Philippines. “But the Collective was never built for creators alone. It was built so more Filipinos could see AI in the context of everyday life—through people they trust, stories they relate to, and examples that show how Copilot can help them create, learn, work, and solve problems responsibly.”


## One Year of Learning, Experimenting, and Creating Together


In its first year, the CCC’s mission moved from idea to action through the creators who carried it into different communities. Across learning spaces, workplace conversations, and education campaigns, members helped make AI feel less abstract and more useful to the people it was meant to serve.


At the YSEALI Bootcamp for Digital Creators, Isa Rodriguez, CJ Salvador, and Jax Reyes brought creator-led perspectives to a regional initiative designed to equip young Southeast Asian leaders with digital storytelling and responsible technology skills. Organized in partnership with the U.S. Department of State through the Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative, the bootcamp gathered 81 Attendees from across the region, representing multiple nations and communities. The initiative provided a platform for CCC members to show how Microsoft 365 and Copilot can support productivity, content creation, and responsible experimentation. Their participation showed how AI literacy can start with people who understand the realities of digital storytelling and can speak to peers in a way that feels grounded, practical, and approachable.


That same role came through in Microsoft’s Work Trend Index campaign, which emphasized that while AI is already embedded in everyday work, the next frontier is helping people and organizations turn individual experimentation into trusted, repeatable, and scalable ways of working. Through this campaign, Trixie Esguerra-Bugia helped make insights on AI adoption, productivity, and the future of work more relatable for everyday professionals and creators. Her own use of Copilot reflects the practical value she helps audiences see: it supports the behind-the-scenes work that makes content creation possible, from organizing shot lists to checking grammar and refining outlines. For creators working as one-human teams, she shows how AI can serve as a digital assistant that brings more structure and confidence to everyday work.


In education, Alvin Santos and Reb Atadero helped bring the same message to Filipino teachers and learners through Microsoft’s campaign in partnership with the Department of Education. Leveraging DepEd’s nationwide network, the campaign showed how free tools such as Copilot Chat and Reading Progress can address classroom needs at scale. In just 21 weeks, it reached 3,431 students across eight regions, analyzed 8,381 reading submissions, trained 2,002 teachers, and achieved 91.5 percent teacher satisfaction. By connecting AI to everyday teaching, literacy, and student support, Alvin and Reb helped frame it as a practical aid for educators and learners alike. Alvin’s own experience reinforces this point: he has used Copilot as a creative sounding board and to develop lesson plans tailored to French non-native English speakers.


The Collective’s work also shows how AI can support more ambitious ideas behind the scenes. Ceej Tantengco-Malolos experienced this while organizing an art exhibit for women’s sports. With Copilot and a small team, she created display mockups, drafted media invitations, and built a promotional plan for an event that might have otherwise felt difficult to take on. Her example adds another layer to the CCC’s first-year story: responsible AI is not only about learning the tool, but using it to bring meaningful ideas to life.


Other members of the Collective echo this sense of possibility. Buji Babiera shared how Copilot helped him gather themes from different parts of the world for a local story under a tight deadline. Abi Maravilla described Copilot as a sounding board that helps simplify the complex and organize ideas without becoming overwhelmed. Andi Lopez shared how it helps turn scattered thoughts into something clearer and more meaningful, while also supporting work such as marketing pitch decks and data analysis for esports commentary.


Seen together, these efforts move the CCC’s story forward from experimentation to impact. In its first year, the Collective helped broaden AI literacy by meeting Filipinos where they are: creators learning to work more efficiently, professionals navigating the future of work, educators looking for practical classroom support, and communities discovering how AI can help them start, organize, teach, create, and solve problems more responsibly.


## The Next Chapter of the Collective


One year in, the Copilot Creators Collective stands as both a milestone and a starting point.


Its first year shows how Filipino creators are already using AI to work more efficiently, think more expansively, and tell stories with greater confidence. It also shows that the future of creativity will not be shaped by technology alone. It will be shaped by people: creators who ask better questions, share what they learn, and use new tools to bring more thoughtful ideas into the world.


“My first year with the Copilot Creator Collective was marked with remarkable firsts. It was my first time working with Microsoft Copilot and AI in general” said Alvin Santos. “And also, my first to be part of a project that fostered long-lasting partnerships with the brand and a thoughtfully curated bunch of amazing content creators. I’m raring to see what’s in store for the 2nd year!”


As the CCC enters its next chapter, its impact will be measured not only by the content its members create, but by how effectively they help more Filipinos understand and use AI in ways that are responsible, useful, and relevant to daily life. The habits they model—responsible experimentation, open collaboration, and the belief that technology works best when it amplifies human imagination—can help shape a more confident and inclusive AI future.


In the Philippines’ new media movement, the future of creativity is already taking shape. Through the Copilot Creators Collective, it is being built together—and shared with the Filipinos it was always meant to empower.
